# Plan for ISSUE-75

Make automatic selection predictable within each repository while preserving the existing eligibility and fenced claim path.

## Shape

**Involved**: selection is centralized, but native sibling ordering needs a tracker read operation and backward-compatible local persistence.

## What we know

- `internal/cli/selection.go:36` defines `pullNextReadyIssue`; it currently iterates `ListIssues` results directly and performs dependency, lease, capability, gate, preflight, and fenced acquisition checks before provisioning.
- Claim, work, and node share this function (`internal/cli/claim.go:47`, `internal/cli/work.go:74`, `internal/cli/node.go:206`). `resolveTargets` in `selection.go` preserves registry order under `--all`.
- `internal/tracker/github.go:429` paginates issue listings without specifying sort order; `internal/tracker/local.go:342` already sorts issue listings by number.
- `internal/tracker/tracker.go:147` exposes `ParentIssueNumber` and `LinkSubIssue`, but no ordered sibling read. GitHub uses native `/parent` and `/sub_issues` endpoints (`github.go:352`, `github.go:370`). Local state records only a child-to-parent map (`local.go:22`), so it cannot recover historical link order.
- Existing CLI fixtures provide local approved WorkUnits and tracker overrides (`internal/cli/cli_test.go:38`); existing selection tests include `TestCLIClaimNextSelectorsAndPreparedWork` and the mislabeled Epic exclusion case near `cli_test.go:709`.
- `Makefile` defines `check` as formatting verification, vet, staticcheck, and race tests. Required build and ordinary test checks are additionally listed in the compiled active policy.

## What we're assuming

- For mixed issues, preserve ascending-number positions and reorder only the positions belonging to siblings of the same epic. This gives sibling precedence without giving every epic a new global priority. Check this explicitly through mixed-order test examples and document it.
- GitHub's paginated native sub-issue listing preserves its displayed sibling order. Verify the endpoint contract during implementation and test ordered page concatenation with an HTTP fake; a live GitHub check is supplementary, not an implementation prerequisite.
- Existing local links have no recoverable native ordering. Use ascending number for those historical siblings; preserve append order for subsequently linked children.

## Open questions

- The criteria do not fully specify standalone-versus-epic precedence. The slot-preserving rule above is the proposed resolution; the mixed-case tests make the result reviewable (e.g. candidates 10, 20, 30 with sibling order 30, 10 become 30, 20, 10).
- Live GitHub ordering after a user drags siblings cannot be exercised without a repository and credentials. Backend tests will verify the read contract and selection tests will verify precedence; optionally confirm UI reorder behavior during PR review without blocking implementation.

## Architectural context and design

Use a selection-local ordering helper, leaving general `ListIssues` behavior and the eligibility/acquisition loop intact. Start with ascending issue numbers, identify native parent epics through tracker reads, then replace each epic's occupied positions with its candidates in native sibling order. Only original ready-list candidates may appear in the result. Filtering remains authoritative in the existing loop, so an earlier blocked sibling never blocks an eligible later sibling.

Do not implement a comparator that uses native order for siblings and issue numbers for unrelated pairs: that relation can be cyclic. Position replacement produces a deterministic permutation. Do not use WorkUnit `parent_issue` text as native-link authority. Cache parent issue/type reads and sibling lists for one selection invocation. Read sibling lists only when multiple candidates share a confirmed epic.

On parent/type lookup errors, warn through `cmd.ErrOrStderr()` and retain numeric ordering for affected candidates. On sibling-list errors or incomplete/duplicate data covering the candidate siblings, warn once for that parent and keep its entire sibling set in numeric order; discard partial page results. Successful reads for other parents may still apply. An absent parent is normal and needs no warning. Propagate context cancellation rather than treating it as a metadata outage. Warnings must remain on stderr even with JSON output and disabled progress.

## Exact touchpoints and implementation sequence

1. In `internal/tracker/tracker.go`, add `ListSubIssues(ctx, parentNumber) ([]*Issue, error)` to `Tracker`, documenting that returned order is native sibling order and grants no eligibility. Update concrete test doubles as needed; embedded `tracker.Tracker` wrappers can inherit it.
2. In `internal/tracker/github.go`, implement `GitHubTracker.ListSubIssues` using the native read endpoint, repository-scoped pagination, existing response conversion and context/error conventions. Add HTTP-fake coverage in `internal/tracker/github_test.go` for preserved ordering, multiple pages, and read errors. Do not create or reorder native links.
3. In `internal/tracker/local.go`, extend `localState` with optional per-parent child order. Initialize it through the existing `withLock` loading path. Implement `LocalTracker.ListSubIssues` under the existing lock. For old state, derive ascending child numbers; on the next new link, persist that baseline plus the appended child. Extend `LinkSubIssue` only to record order atomically alongside its existing parent update; preserve idempotence, cycle checks, and safefs writes. Add local round-trip, legacy-state, reverse-link-order, and idempotence tests in `internal/tracker/github_test.go`, alongside existing local native-link tests. No separate reordering API or migration command.
4. In `internal/cli/selection.go`, add `orderReadyIssues` implementing the permutation above and call it after listing candidates, before the existing attempt loop. Keep repository traversal, eligibility checks, preflight errors, claim fencing, retries, and worktree setup unchanged. Metadata never adds a candidate.
5. Create `internal/cli/selection_test.go`: fake tracker tests for ordering and warnings, plus command-level cases using the existing fixture and `trackerOverride` to demonstrate actual eligible selection through all three entry points and unchanged `--all` traversal. Include dependency-blocked, active-lease, human-gate, capability, Epic, and PR-open exclusions.
6. Update `docs/developer.md` at the next-task and worker-pool sections, and the relevant selection descriptions in `README.md`'s quick-reference table. Explain numeric order, native sibling precedence, mixed-case behavior, warning/fallback, unchanged eligibility and repository traversal. Preserve existing visuals and real command flags.
7. Run the TEST_PLAN checks, resolve failures within this scope, and record actual results during implementation. No production changes, staging, claim-bound validation, or publication occur in this planning phase.

## Scope boundaries

No priority labels, Projects fields, new eligibility rules, cross-repository ranking, native link creation feature, protected harness changes, or workflow changes. The tracker additions serve only the requested ordering. No split is needed; native read support and selection are coupled parts of this outcome.
